articles.title: GOP lawmakers urge Trump to reimpose sanctions on Russian-owned Serbian refinery
articles.summary: A pair of House Republicans are urging the Trump administration to resume sanctions on a Russian-owned refinery in Serbia, according to a letter obtained exclusively by The Hill. The GOP criticism marks another instance of growing Republican pushback against the president’s foreign policy actions. Reps. Joe Wilson (R-S.C.) and Keith Self (R-Texas), staunch allies of…
articles.body:
A pair of House Republicans are urging the Trump administration to resume sanctions on a Russian-owned refinery in Serbia, according to a letter obtained exclusively by The Hill. The GOP criticism marks another instance of growing Republican pushback against the president’s foreign policy actions.

Reps. Joe Wilson (R-S.C.) and Keith Self (R-Texas), staunch allies of President Trump, sent a letter to the Treasury Department on Friday arguing against extending sanctions relief provided to Serbia’s Russian-owned energy company, NIS.

“We write to you to respectfully request that you reconsider extending any additional temporary licenses allowing Serbia’s Oil Industry of Serbia (NIS) to continue operating despite U.S. sanctions related to its Russian ownership,” the lawmakers wrote. The letter was addressed to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

The U.S. has repeatedly issued sanctions waivers for NIS since the company was blacklisted in January 2025 after sanctions related to Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

NIS supplies 80 percent of Serbia’s energy needs but is majority owned by U.S.-sanctioned Russian energy giants Gazprom Neft and Gazprom.

Last week, NIS applied for another waiver ahead of a Sept. 30 deadline, when their most recent is set to expire.

Wilson and Self raise concern that the waivers are enabling NIS to drag out negotiations to sell off the Russian stake in the company. In January, Hungarian-based company MOL announced it had reached a deal with Gazprom Neft to take over its majority share in NIS, but it has not yet concluded.

“Negotiations over the final purchase agreement remain ongoing, and MOL has sought continued authorization from your department to continue to operate despite limited progress,” the lawmakers wrote.

“Furthermore, Serbia continues to maintain close political and economic ties with Russia and, unlike most European countries, has not imposed sanctions on Moscow following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022,” they added.

The rare GOP pushback comes as Republicans are increasingly speaking out over Trump’s handling of foreign affairs. This includes concern over the president inviting Putin to a major economic summit in Miami at the end of the year, despite the ongoing war with Ukraine; increasing GOP criticism over the course of the seven-month war with Iran, which has upended global energy supplies and triggered rising diesel and gasoline prices; and outrage over Trump’s lavish hosting of Chinese President Xi Jinping .

articles.title: After hydrogen train, India’s first LNG-powered train has been flagged off from Ahmedabad; Amit Shah says railways is cutting diesel, targets net zero by 2030
articles.summary: Within months of launching its first hydrogen train, Indian Railways has now rolled out its first LNG train.
articles.body: Within months of launching its first hydrogen train, Indian Railways has now rolled out its first LNG train. Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday flagged off India’s first LNG train from Sabarmati station in Gujarat.The move is part of the national transporter’s broader push to reduce carbon emissions and move towards more sustainable modes of transport.At the event, Shah also flagged off a WAG-12 electric locomotive from Sabarmati station. Several railway projects of over Rs 1500 crore in total were also dedicated to the nation, inaugurated or taken up for foundation stone laying. These included railway line doubling projects, the Kavach train protection system, automatic signalling works and a maintenance shed for WAG-12 electric locomotives.India’s first LNG trainShah said that the LNG-powered train will make a significant contribution to environmental conservation in the years to come.The LNG-powered train operates on a dual-fuel diesel-plus-LNG system developed for its Driving Power Cars (DPCs).At the Sabarmati Integrated Coaching Depot, two DPCs, each with a power capacity of 1,400 HP, have been modified to operate using the dual-fuel technology. The system allows the locomotives to use LNG along with diesel.The two converted DPCs have undergone more than 2,000 km of field trials to evaluate the technology's performance and reliability under operating conditions, reports suggest.Also Read | Why India's first hydrogen train is special - explainedThe dual-fuel arrangement allows LNG to substitute for around 40 per cent of diesel consumption. Trial data released by the Railways indicates that the technology could lower fuel costs as well as emissions, including carbon dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter.The technology also gives the engine the flexibility to operate on either LNG or diesel based on fuel availability. This allows the train to continue operating without being dependent on a single fuel source, reports say.While using LNG to replace part of the diesel requirement, the system has been designed to preserve the conventional diesel engine's power and operational capabilities.Each converted DPC is equipped with an LNG tank holding around 2,200 litres. The tank can accommodate approximately 850-900 kg of usable LNG.A full tank of LNG is expected to support around 1,600 km of operations, thereby reducing the frequency with which the train needs to refuel.Indian Railways targets net zeroAmit Shah also highlighted several infrastructure and operational changes. He said 97% of bio-toilets had been installed in trains under the Modi government, while 87% of LBH coaches produced during the Prime Minister's tenure were manufactured in India.According to Shah, railway electrification increased by 70%, the budget allocated for railway safety rose by 67% and locomotive production capacity expanded by 66% during Modi's tenure."Modi solidified the concept of Make in India, the concept of self-reliant India, and this is the result of it. In 2015-16, Railways used 293 crore litres of diesel. By 2024-25 it will be 108 crore litres, and by 2030 it will be reduced to zero. We will save currency. This is a great achievement which does not come to people's attention," Shah said.He further pointed to the pace of railway electrification, saying that the annual addition of electrified railway tracks had risen from 75 km in 2010-11 to 7,188 km in 2023-24. Shah said the task, which he described as difficult, had been completed smoothly."Railways has completed 99.6 percent electrification. We will complete the remaining 0.3 percent. Electrification is 92 percent in China, 68 percent in Spain, 60 in France, and 49 percent in a small country like Britain. We will move ahead by ensuring it is 100 percent in India," he said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: AI agents promise to do everything for you. There may be a big wrinkle in that plan
articles.summary: Meta wants its new Muse AI agent to be the gateway to users’ digital lives. But that all depends on whether popular apps and services are willing to give it the keys.
articles.body: Meta wants its new Muse AI agent to be the gateway to users’ digital lives. But that all depends on whether popular apps and services are willing to give it the keys. Agents go a step beyond how most people have used AI up to this point. Instead of simply answering questions, organizing emails and creating images, they can take multistep actions on the internet. They can compare prices, shop, book reservations and fill out forms, if the companies that sell things and take reservations allow them. That change may spark a new battle over the future of internet services. Amazon recently blocked Muse’s AI agent from accessing its store, and some experts say the move could foreshadow a dilemma for online businesses. If more people use AI agents for daily tasks, businesses may need to make a critical choice: Partner with companies like Meta and risk their own platforms possibly becoming irrelevant. Or potentially miss out on reaching billions of customers through what may be the future of how people get things done. Shares of Airbnb, Expedia, and Trip Advisor fell around 5% last week after Meta announced new updates for its Muse agent. Meta’s Muse makes waves The idea of AI agents isn’t new; OpenAI, Google, Apple and Amazon, along with Meta, have been working towards this future for years and have gradually rolled out new agent-like features. But Muse caught on almost immediately, shooting to the top of the free app chart on Apple’s App Store 10 days after its September 8 debut. Meta owns Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp, and its pervasive internet presence — along with the app’s relatively easy interface — largely drove the AI agent’s success. Compared to other tech giants, Meta has done a better job at showing Muse’s capabilities to consumers, according to Francisco Jeronimo, an analyst with technology market research firm International Data Corporation. “Others have not been so vocal about using the agents to be able to shop as Meta has been with Muse, and I think that’s the main difference,” he said. Meta has partnered with Walmart, GameStop, Sephora, Expedia, OpenTable and Shopify to incorporate their services into the Muse app. But e-commerce juggernaut Amazon refused to play ball with Meta. Amazon blocked the agent, saying it was not given notice or a choice about whether its store should be available through Muse. The company also cited concerns around how Amazon account data and credentials would be handled, and said agents don’t offer Amazon’s personalized recommendations. “We think it’s fairly straightforward that third-party applications that offer to make purchases on behalf of customers from other businesses should operate openly and respect service provider decisions about whether or not to participate,” Amazon said in a statement to CNN. Online restaurant reservations platform Resy also told CNN that it “does not currently permit unapproved third-party bots or agents” to access its service. The platform locked a user’s account following attempts by his AI agent, a separate assistant called Instinct, to book hundreds of tables per hour earlier this month. “Unapproved automated activity can introduce risks to the platform and compromise a fair reservation experience for diners,” the company said. CNN was able to book a reservation through Muse after providing login information, like a phone number and confirmation code. Resy integrates with ChatGPT and Claude and said it will “continue to evaluate opportunities” as AI agents progress. Risks and rewards of agents Amazon may be an outlier. But some experts say AI agents pose real risks that could give many online service providers some pause before allowing agents to use their platforms. For one, there’s the potential decrease in web traffic if tasks are primarily handled on the AI agent apps. Brands could also lose the ability to learn about customer shopping habits or further entice users into additional purchases with in-app promotions or product recommendations. “You browse Amazon for that thing that you’re looking for, but then you also see other things that you know you may end up buying,” said Mandeep Singh, a senior industry analyst for Bloomberg Intelligence. Additionally, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Wednesday that the company eventually plans to charge a commission for transactions made through Muse. This means other companies may lose a cut of their sales. And it’s not just shopping and reservation apps that may be impacted. AI agents are generally good at tasks that require research, like comparing insurance policies or mobile carrier plans. This could potentially make it easier for users to switch plans to land a better deal. But the upside could also be huge. Muse has already been downloaded more than 2.5 million times, according to market intelligence firm Sensor Tower, giving businesses visibility to millions of people around the world. That could make Muse especially appealing to smaller and mid-sized brands, like those who work with Shopify. That was part of the appeal for travel platform Expedia, which chose to allow AI agents because it wants “to show up wherever travelers are searching,” Kathryn Heinz, Expedia’s vice president of enterprise alliances and AI, said in a comment to CNN. She added that about two-thirds of Expedia’s traffic comes through its own platforms. And some might see it as a move to future-proof their business. “I think long term, that’s exactly what we will see: the AI platforms to become the layer and the main interface for most of us when we are when we are shopping,” International Data Corporation’s Jeronimo said.

articles.title: US and China agree to cut tariffs on $60 billion worth of goods, from coal to toys
articles.summary: The United States and China have agreed to slash tariffs on $60 billion worth of goods, deepening efforts to stabilize a frequently testy relationship.
articles.body: The United States and China have agreed to slash tariffs on $60 billion worth of goods, deepening efforts to stabilize a frequently testy relationship. The tariff relief extends to an array of products, from US coal and agricultural products to made-in-China toys, car seats and holiday decorations. The announcement from the White House late Sunday followed a highly anticipated meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Washington last week. The White House said that under a so-called “30-for-30” framework, each country would be allowed to import “non-sensitive” goods worth $30 billion from the other at reduced tariff rates. The more favorable tariff treatment followed recommendations from the US-China Board of Trade and would improve market access for about 30% of US exports to China, US trade representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement Sunday. “The Trump Administration will continue to pursue fair, balanced, and reciprocal trade with China by ensuring compliance with commitments on agricultural and energy purchases, pursuing balanced trade in non-sensitive goods, and securing market access for American farmers, manufacturers, businesses, and workers,” he added. The Chinese list of US products that will be subject to lower tariffs covers 1,619 items, including corn, wheat, frozen meat, seafood, wood products, cosmetics and medical devices, according to a list published by the White House. US soybeans were not included, a blow to struggling American farmers who have been collateral damage from a years-long tit-for-tat trade war between the two countries. The White House also said that China would import at least 10 million metric tons of coal from the United States in 2027 and again in 2028. Previous commitments to import certain quantities of goods, such as agricultural products, have not always been met in full, however. The US list of Chinese imports covers 77 items, including toys, tableware, kitchen accessories, curtains, electric shavers and inflatable balls. The Chinese commerce ministry said the agreement would “further stabilize” China-US economic and trade relations and “create favorable conditions” for the export of relevant Chinese products to the United States. US trade deficit with China shrinking The announcement comes after the US and China agreed ahead of Xi’s visit to press pause on escalating tariff measures until January 10. The trade truce – which sets tariff levels at 30% on Chinese goods and 10% on US goods – has been extended multiple times since May 2025, when the two countries met in Geneva for negotiations. The goods listed Sunday, however, will likely be carved out of future tariff measures. Trump has used tariffs to narrow the US trade deficit with China – or the difference between what America exports to China and what it imports from China – prompting Chinese exporters to send more goods elsewhere, including to Europe. In an interview with CNBC on Friday, Greer said the deficit on goods trade with China had fallen 40% since Trump took office and was on track to reach $140 billion this year. Data from the US Census Bureau showed the deficit amounted to around $295 billion in 2024. Beyond trade, the two countries also agreed to establish a bilateral communication channel to discuss any artificial intelligence-related “incidents,” according to the White House. The White House said Xi and Trump agreed to use the term “super intelligence” rather than “artificial intelligence” to describe the emerging technology, and that the two sides had established the. U.S.-China Super Intelligence Dialogue to exchange views on risks and benefits related to AI. The next exchange will occur by November 2026. – CNN’s Stephanie Yang, Issy Ronald and Sylvie Zhang contributed reporting.

articles.title: The national debt should be the number one issue in this year’s election
articles.summary: The federal government’s spending plans should mirror the average American family’s plan.
articles.body:
I cannot understand why the national debt is not the number one issue being debated today by federal politicians when campaigning during the time before the midterm Congressional elections.

We hear much discussion about the Iran War, gas prices, inflation in general, Hassan Piker’s influence on Democrats, immigration policy and health care. But our nation is a great risk of an economic meltdown that will sideline these issues if the federal government does not get its debt under control. Our national debt is a national security issue that must be addressed before it is too late.

Our federal spending has soared over the years and outpaced revenue. According to the Department of Treasury , spending for fiscal 2025 (which ended last Sept. 30) will exceed $7 trillion. Compare that number to the pre-COVID level spending in fiscal 2019 that was $5.6 trillion. As a percentage of Gross Domestic Product, the percentage of federal spending has risen by 2 points to 23 percent. So almost one quarter of the spending in this economy comes from a government that borrows to make ends meet.

One problem that has emerged over the years is that the federal government never stopped the excessive spending during the COVID years. In fiscal 2020, federal spending hit $8.2 trillion followed by fiscal 2021 where spending stayed at $8.1 trillion. It did come down a bit in the year following 2022, but has never lowered to the levels before COVID with regard to the top line number and percentage of GDP.

Some politicians have noticed. Rep. Chip Roy (R-Texas) posted on X last year, “Pre-COVID, the government spent $4.4 trillion. Six years later, we are spending $7 TRILLION. For this republic to continue standing, this level of spending from our government must decrease.”

My former boss, Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.) posted on X recently, “6 years later, we still haven’t returned to pre-COVID spending levels. How does that even make sense?” It makes no sense, because the American people have yet to rise up and elect politicians who make it a priority to cut federal spending.

Cutting spending may seem difficult, yet getting back to pre-COVID level spending makes sense to most.

Lack of taxation is not the problem. On the revenue side, again using government statistics, the federal government took in $4.9 trillion in 2025 versus $4.4 trillion in 2019. There is a big gulf between what the government takes in in taxes an spends. Taking more money from the American people will not solve the problem of increased government spending — it will merely give more money to bureaucrats to spend as they wish without consequences.

The federal budget is a mess. When one looks at the budget for fiscal 2026, the second ranked spending program is interest on the debt. At 15 percent of the whole, that is less than outlays for Social Security, but it is larger than outlays for Medicare, health programs and national defense. For this year, it is estimated that the federal government will rack up $1 trillion in just interest on the national debt that just exceeded $40 trillion collectively for the first time in U.S. history.

For those worried about government mandatory spending programs continuing, they will not continue if the federal government becomes insolvent.

There are solutions, such as Paul’s Six Penny Plan. As the Mises Institute explains it, “Each year for the next five years, Congress would reduce the federal budget by six percent from the previous year’s budget. In five years, the annual budget would be in balance, and the total federal debt will be on a path to being paid off.” The cuts are across the board, with each agency deciding where to make the cuts.

The federal government’s spending plans should mirror the average American family’s plan. Families spent far more and lost revenues during COVID, yet they still had to balance their family budgets. We should ask the same for the federal government.

Left-leaning politicians will yell, “Tax The Rich!” as a solution. That will not not balance the budget, but it would serve to transform the U.S. into the very sort of socialist country innovators flee. It wll mean the next AI, iPhone or personal computer will be created in Singapore or some other nation that respects private property and the free market.

During this debate to elect Members of Congress in the House and Senate, not much will be said of federal spending. Nobody will propose a plan to cut back on the size and scope of the federal government. We need more Rand Pauls and Chip Roys in the federal government who recognize that spending is a problem and are willing to do something about it.

Brian Darling is former counsel to Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.).

articles.title: Nvidia launches new tool to keep AI agents from going rogue
articles.summary: Chipmaker Nvidia said Monday it is introducing a new software platform to address concerns about artificial intelligence agents that have “gone rogue” and operated outside human control.
articles.body: Chipmaker Nvidia said Monday it is introducing a new software platform to address concerns about artificial intelligence agents that have “gone rogue” and operated outside human control. “Today, with over 100 industry partners, we introduced the NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang wrote in a post on X Monday. Nvidia (NVDA) says its technology will enable companies to monitor every action undertaken by an AI agent, as well as enforce policies. “AI’s extraordinary potential for society will only be realized if we solve AI safety,” Huang added in a statement. “As we continue to discover the frontier of AI capabilities, we must accelerate discovery at the frontier of AI safety.” The announcement comes in the wake of a series of incidents in which AI systems hacked into both corporate and government systems without being told to do so. OpenAI said Saturday that it was pausing development on its latest models after one accessed the internet without authorization. Top AI executives, like OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, have repeatedly called for international regulations to constrain the systems, and some researchers have warned that AI may even present a threat to human life. But Huang has dismissed those concerns, calling any existential threat overblown, and said last week that any regulations should promote the growth of the AI industry, not hinder it. “If they believe their company is out of control, then get the company under control,” Huang told CNN’s Anderson Cooper on Friday. Nvidia also announced Monday that it will buy back an additional $150 billion worth of its shares, on top of an $85 billion share repurchase it already had underway. The company said this would be the largest single corporate share repurchase ever. Apple previously held the record with a $110 billion repurchase announced in 2024. Shares of Nvidia rose 3% in early trading on the news. Nvidia has a current market cap of $5.4 trillion, making it the most valuable company on the planet. “Our cash generation gives us the capacity to invest in the technologies that advance this transformation and return capital to shareholders,” said the company in a statement. “This authorization reflects our confidence in the long-term opportunity ahead.” A spate of incidents Concerns about AI agents going rogue started to gain traction this summer when OpenAI disclosed one of its experimental AI models left a test environment with no human direction and hacked its way onto the systems of a different company, Hugging Face, while trying to “cheat” on a cybersecurity test. Last week, the Australian government said that an OpenAI agent accessed both “public and non-public files” in the country’s Medicare statistics database in June. AI research lab Transluce also said Wednesday that it had detected AI agents going rogue on several occasions going back to at least March, predating previously known hacking incidents. Then on Friday, OpenAI disclosed that its agents accessed publicly available data from the Commerce Department’s Census Bureau using login credentials it found online, and separately shared public data from the Securities and Exchange Commission on another website. OpenAI’s agents attempted but failed to gain access to the Education Department and gather data from its civil rights office, according to the report. And in a separate incident disclosed Saturday, the company said that it was pausing development of its most capable models after one escaped a testing environment and accessed the open internet – despite new security protocols put into place following the Hugging Face attack. President Donald Trump has repeatedly dismissed concerns about AI as a “SICK conspiracy” and a “HOAX,” and has also said he is creating an “AI Force” to enable the growth of the industry. While Trump and Huang speak regularly, Trump had dinner Sunday night with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who has regularly called for stricter limits on the technology. This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.title: Nvidia announces jaw-dropping $150 billion stock buyback, largest single authorization in history
articles.summary: The valuation on Nvidia is too appetizing for CEO Jensen Huang to ignore any longer.
articles.body:
The valuation on Nvidia ( NVDA ) is too appetizing for CEO Jensen Huang to ignore any longer.

The king of AI chips revealed a stunning new $150 billion stock buyback plan on Monday — the largest share repurchase authorization increase in history. It brings the company's total buyback authorization to $235 billion.

"NVIDIA's growth is being driven by a once-in-a-generation platform shift to AI and accelerated computing," Huang said in a statement. "Our cash generation gives us the capacity to invest in the technologies that advance this transformation and return capital to shareholders. This authorization reflects our confidence in the long-term opportunity ahead."

Huang likely sees a great moment to buy back Nvidia shares on the cheap, ahead of further acceleration in AI development.

Nvidia's forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple has declined steadily since August 2024, when artificial intelligence began to take hold, unleashing a boom in the company's stock price and earnings growth.

The decline has only accelerated this year despite a series of strong quarters.

The forward P/E ratio for Nvidia currently stands at 24 times, not too far removed from the S&P 500's ( ^GSPC ) 20-times multiple, despite the company being one of the fastest-growing companies in corporate America.

articles.title: Why diesel price and Treasury yield relief would be huge wins for stocks
articles.summary: Something to watch underneath the surface of a hot market.
articles.body:
If there is relief to be had from surging gas prices and rising Treasury yields soon, it could open the door for another thrust higher for the market.

That's a big if , but it's one to keep an eye on just like the power brokers on Wall Street.

"While AI strength has kept the headline S&P 500 relatively resilient, the median stock in the index trades 16% below its 52-week high, dragging market breadth to its lowest level since the Dot-Com Bubble," Goldman Sachs strategist Ben Snider said. "Together, these factors indicate the potential for both broad market upside and a 'catch-up' from recent laggards if macro uncertainty declines."

The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) continues to trade near record highs despite elevated oil prices and surging bond yields , underpinned by robust corporate earnings growth this year.

Analysts project aggregate third quarter S&P 500 earnings growth of nearly 29% year over year, providing a strong fundamental floor that absorbs elevated discount rates.

Further helping the S&P 500 is the return of the "Magnificent Seven" trade amid AI optimism, which has lit a renewed flame under names like Meta ( META ) and Nvidia ( NVDA ).

Outside of the AI complex, that's where things get hairy for the S&P 500, as there are a host of laggards.

McDonald's ( MCD ), PepsiCo ( PEP ), Lowe's ( LOW ), and Nike ( NKE ) are all hovering around 52-week lows.

Goldman's Snider is banking on improved market breadth supporting a higher S&P 500 in the next 12 months. He expects the S&P 500 to rise 13% to 8,700 over that span.

articles.title: Apple ordered to pay $5.7bn after losing vibration tech patent suit
articles.summary: Audio firm Taction Technology claimed Apple infringed its patents for tech used to power device vibrations.
articles.body:
Apple has been ordered to pay $5.7bn (£4.3bn) in damages after a US jury found it had used another firm's tech without permission.

Audio firm Taction Technology claimed in 2021 that Apple had infringed two of its patents for haptics systems, which enable vibrations for actions such as receiving a message or pressing a button.

This tech is built into devices like the iPhone and Apple Watch.

Apple said it had not used Taction's vibration tech and would appeal the verdict.

"While we thank the jury for their consideration, we strongly disagree with today's verdict and the damages awarded, which are entirely unsupported by the facts," it said.

"Apple's Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction's technology, which Taction's own testing of Apple's products confirmed during trial."

Haptics allow people to interact with devices by simulating the sense of touch or feel through vibrations.

They have become a hallmark of modern devices, with smartphones, watches and video game controllers among those containing small motors that move in response to specific electronic signals.

Apple's "Taptic Engine" system - enabling haptic feedback in its devices - first debuted with the Apple Watch in 2014.

Since then, it has improved its underlying system, and with that expanded haptics in its devices.

Taction, which makes headphones and gaming headsets, claimed in 2021 that these improvements infringed patents it was issued in 2020.

It wrote in its complaint that by producing better haptic vibrations in its devices, Apple had been able to improve its overall user experience.

As such, the tech giant had been "capitalising on Taction's innovation and success by selling devices that infringe [its] patents", Taction said.

It also accused Apple of using its inventions "without license or authority".

A San Diego judge ruled in 2023 that Apple did not infringe upon Taction's patents.

However, an appeal was subsequently taken up by a federal appeal circuit - resulting in a September jury trial at the US District Court for the Southern District of California which found in its favour.

In Friday's verdict , jurors did not find that Apple had infringed the patents in question willingly.

It marks one of many similar lawsuits the tech giant has defended itself against in recent years.

In November 2025 a judge ordered Apple to pay $634m to medical tech firm Masimo after a jury found it had infringed a patent for blood-oxygen reading tech.

articles.title: China and U.S. agree to tariff cuts on $60 billion of goods including agriculture, household items
articles.summary: China and the U.S agreed to cut tariffs on $60 billion worth of goods, ranging from U.S. corn to cosmetics and from Chinese household appliances to toys.
articles.body: China and the United States have agreed to cut tariffs imposed on $60 billion worth of goods imported from each other, on an array of products ranging from U.S. corn to cosmetics, and from Chinese household appliances to toys. Under the U.S.-China Board of Trade, both countries have each recommended $30 billion of trade in non-sensitive goods for more favourable tariff treatment, United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement on Sunday. For the United States, that was “unlocking improved market access” for about 30% of U.S. exports to China, he said. The reciprocal tariff reduction as well as an extension of a trade truce were among the key takeaways from the second summit this year between Chinese President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump, hosted in Washington last week. One of two lists from the White House showed that China planned to trim duties on a variety of US agricultural goods including corn, wheat, sorghum, meat, dairy, vegetable oils and meals. It did not include soybeans. Beijing will also look to reduce levies on American fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices. In another list were Washington’s reciprocal tariff cuts for Chinese small appliances such as coffee makers and toasters, tableware, blankets and bed linens. The lists also included toys, fireworks, artificial flowers, Christmas tree lamps and other holiday decorations, and children’s car seats. Longer trade truce China’s commerce ministry said on Monday a two-month extension of a trade truce with the United States through to Jan. 10 would provide room for both sides to evaluate their ongoing arrangement to resolve economic and trade issues, while considering how to advance on those fronts. The extension also provides a “relatively stable and predictable policy environment” for cooperation among companies and continued active discussions. Both sides will hold regular talks on potential investment opportunities and barriers, enhancing policy transparency and predictability, and responding to enterprises’ concerns, the ministry said. Stocks fell sharply in China on Monday, with investors having few concrete details to cheer from the leaders’ summit and underlying tensions resurfacing. Technology stocks fell on a bipartisan U.S. push to ban Chinese components from data centres and the benchmark blue-chip index .CSI300 slid more than 2% to a one-year low. Agriculture and coal China’s choice of products for tariff cuts looks designed to help Beijing meet what the White House says is a $17 billion commitment to buy agricultural goods. China has already resumed large-scale buying of American soybeans under a deal struck last year to buy 25 million metric tons annually. Both countries will set up an agriculture working group under a trade council, which will hold its first meeting before the year ends to discuss two-way market access and regulation, the commerce ministry said. The presidential summit also yielded an agreement for China to import 10 million metric tons of coal annually from the United States in 2027 and 2028, the White House release showed. That amount roughly equals 2% of China’s coal imports each year. Liquefied natural gas and oil were not on the list. “Importing U.S. coal is not only a beneficial supplement to China’s domestic coal market, but also brings stable economic income and employment to the U.S. coal industry,” the Chinese ministry said. AI, financial firms and direct flights On artificial intelligence, both sides have agreed on a communication channel for incidents and will hold a follow-up dialogue by the end of November. China will also examine and approve foreign financial services institutions, including those with American capital, to conduct business and open branches in China. There will also be continued communication on increasing flights between China and the United States, the ministry statement said.

articles.title: New SNAP benefit amounts take effect Oct. 1: Here’s how much
articles.summary: Starting Oct. 1, new eligibility rules and updated benefit amounts will take effect for the estimated 37 million Americans receiving SNAP assistance.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – Starting Oct. 1, new eligibility rules and updated benefit amounts will take effect for the estimated 37 million Americans receiving SNAP assistance.

The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), formerly known as Food Stamps, helps lower-income households afford groceries. Every month, participants see their benefit amount loaded onto an EBT debit card.

The amount recipients receive monthly is about to change thanks to an annual cost-of-living adjustment . In most cases, the maximum allotment is increasing slightly to keep up with inflation. Residents of one state, however, are seeing their benefits decline.

Income eligibility is also changing with new maximums depending on state, age and disability status.

How much someone receives in SNAP benefits depends largely on their household income and assets.

Generally, you qualify for at least some assistance if your gross monthly income is 130% or less than the federal poverty level. Starting in October, that number equals $1,729 as an individual or $3,575 as a family of four. The net income limits are lower: $1,330 for an individual or $2,750 for a family of four.

For able-bodied, non-elderly SNAP recipients, the new gross income limits are:

Different rules and limits are in place for households that have someone who is elderly or disabled. See the income limits for all situations in the new guidance here .

The asset limit will remain unchanged this year. It’s set at $3,000 for most households, or $4,750 in households where someone is disabled or 60 and older.

The maximum SNAP monthly allotment is changing to keep up with the rising cost of food .

The maximum amount a household receives depends on the state they live in. For a family of four living in the 48 contiguous U.S. states or Washington, D.C., the new benefit limit is $1,023.

The changes to maximum benefit amounts for SNAP recipients in the 48 contiguous states, plus D.C., are detailed in the chart below:

Alaska, Hawaii, Guam and the U.S. Virgin Islands have higher maximums due to the high cost of groceries in those places. A family of four in rural Alaska, for example, will be getting as much as $2,027 starting in October.

In Hawaii, benefits are actually decreasing slightly. A household of four in Hawaii will now have a maximum benefit of $1,655. (See more details about the changes in Alaska, Hawaii and U.S. territories here .)

The change in benefit amounts are roughly in line with inflation. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics , the cost of food at home has gone up about 2.7% year-over-year. Overall inflation is at 3.4%.

The new benefit amounts and eligibility requirements are in place from Oct. 1, 2026, through Sept. 30, 2027.

articles.title: Qué es el 'Triqbriq', el sistema de construcción modular al más puro estilo 'Lego' con el que se levantan casas en Alemania
articles.standfirst: La arquitectura circular adopta un novedoso sistema modular que elimina pegamentos y metales
articles.summary: La arquitectura circular adopta un novedoso sistema modular que elimina pegamentos y metales
articles.body: El sector de la construcción está siempre en busca de nuevos métodos más sostenibles para sustituir materiales tradicionales como el hormigón o el ladrillo. En este contexto de innovación constante, surge una alternativa alemana que promete revolucionar la forma en que levantamos y concebimos nuestros edificios. La clave reside en un enfoque profundamente circular que reduce el impacto ambiental. El sistema es similar a los míticos 'Legos', pero en una dimensión mayor ya que utiliza bloques micromodulares de madera maciza, denominados BRIQs, diseñados para interconectarse de manera rápida e intuitiva. Lo revolucionario de esta metodología es que se basa en un montaje completamente en seco, garantizando una ejecución precisa en el sitio de obra. Al prescindir totalmente de pegamentos químicos, uniones metálicas estructurales y adhesivos, el proceso elimina la generación de residuos contaminantes durante la edificación. Además del aspecto logístico, el proyecto destaca por su elevado compromiso medioambiental y su gestión responsable de los recursos forestales. La materia prima proviene de madera de menor calidad comercial, material recuperado o árboles afectados por plagas y eventos climáticos adversos. De esta forma, lo que antes se descartaba se convierte ahora en un elemento estructural de altísimo valor que almacena carbono de la atmósfera. Uno de los pilares más potentes de esta propuesta es la capacidad de desmontaje integral de sus estructuras. Puesto que las piezas no están pegadas ni soldadas, cualquier edificación puede desarmarse por completo al terminar su ciclo de vida útil sin dañar los componentes. Los bloques quedan intactos y listos para reintegrarse inmediatamente en nuevas construcciones, cerrando así un ciclo perfecto de economía circular. Gracias al uso de componentes prefabricados con alta precisión robótica, los tiempos de ejecución en obra se reducen drásticamente en comparación con la edificación convencional. Esta tecnología combina eficiencia técnica, máximo aprovechamiento forestal y un compromiso real con la descarbonización del planeta, demostrando que es posible construir de forma limpia, duradera y responsable.

articles.title: Why you may get 3 paychecks in October, and how it could impact your 2027
articles.summary: The start of October may feel pretty unremarkable for you, but depending on when you get paid, it may be an extra special month.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – The start of October may feel pretty unremarkable for you, but depending on when you get paid, it may be an extra special month.

Generally speaking, four months out of the year have five Fridays. If you are paid every other week, that means two months in which you get an “extra” paycheck (if you’re paid weekly, you get an extra paycheck in all four months).

We have already seen three three-payday months in 2026: April, May, and July .

That means October will be the final triple paycheck month until 2027, which will prove to be an interesting year for some.

Will you get 3 (or 5) paychecks in October?

If you got an “extra” paycheck in July, no. If you did in May, yes.

Can’t remember? Take a look at when you were last paid. If you were just paid on Friday, Sept. 25, you will not see an additional paycheck in October. If you haven’t been paid since Sept. 18, you will get that third or fifth payday.

Those who are paid biweekly and receiving only two checks in October have to wait until January for their next triple-payday month, but it may be worth it.

The typical year has four months with an extra Friday because 52 weeks can’t be evenly spread across the 12 months of a year.

Because January 1 falls on a Friday, there will be five months with five Fridays: January, April, July, October, and December.

If you are paid every other week and receive only two paychecks in October 2026, you can expect three paychecks in January, July, and December. If you get three paychecks next month, April and October will be your triple-payday months in 2027.

Regardless of when your paychecks arrive, it’s important to note that it isn’t like you won the lottery . You’re still earning the wage that you should expect to earn.

Financial experts even encourage treating the additional paycheck as a normal paycheck. If your budget is balanced for the month, they recommend putting the additional funds toward paying down a debt, setting aside for another month, or tucking it away in your savings.

articles.title: Iraq looks for oil export alternatives to the troubled Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: The continued blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has forced Iraq to look for alternatives to export its oil.
articles.body:
In his speech at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Friday, Iraq’s Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi spoke about the challenges his country has faced amid the ongoing war between the United States and Iran.

The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has cut off Iraq’s sea-based trade, including oil exports – a lifeline for the country.

Iraq has been unable to export about 90 percent of its oil via the Gulf and has lost $60bn in oil revenues since the war began.

“We are watching with concern the fallout over shipping and maritime freedom in the Strait of Hormuz, which has triggered a crisis of rising global oil price,” al-Zaidi told the assembly.

It is evident that the financial crisis caused by lost oil receipts has presented the Iraqi government with a mountain of challenges.

Oil revenues make up about 90 percent of Iraq’s federal budget and the decline in exports has impacted the government’s ability to pay salaries and prompted protests in Baghdad.

The Iraqi government is looking at a range of austerity measures to deal with the deficit, but they are unpopular with the population.

Al-Zaidi suggested that boosting oil production in the coming years and diversifying export routes could increase government revenues. That could be achieved by developing existing export channels, such as the Iraq–Turkiye Pipeline (ITP), or establishing new ones with Jordan and Syria.

But none of the proposals provide a quick solution to Iraq’s economic woes, with the Strait of Hormuz – for long the main gateway for Iraqi oil to the rest of the world – remaining effectively closed for the foreseeable future.

Iraqi political and security analyst Sarmad Al-Bayati told Al Jazeera that the lack of quick solutions for Iraq’s oil export conundrum is a major problem for the country.

“At present, the only option is to export through the Strait of Hormuz, which depends primarily on the situation in the strait,” Al-Bayati told Al Jazeera.

“Other alternatives, such as oil exporting routes through Syria or Turkiye, or even future plans to extend a pipeline through Jordan, are unrealistic and impractical at the moment, offering no real solutions to Iraq’s current crisis if the situation remains as it is in the strait.”

Iraq has relied on inefficient ship-to-ship transfers to get some oil out via Basra and other Gulf ports, with small boats carrying cargo through the Strait of Hormuz under US military protection.

Ali Nazar, the head of Iraqi Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO), told a recent session in the Iraqi parliament that Iraq’s oil export capacity was 4.2 million barrels in September, but actual average exports were much lower at 2.5 million barrels. Before the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, Iraq was exporting 3.5 million barrels per day.

SOMO is offering discounts of $26.5 for each barrel for medium oil and about $28 for heavy oil, he added. Despite that, the company is struggling to find buyers due to continued attacks on vessels transiting the strait.

“It isn’t an easy task. It is extremely difficult. It requires high-level coordination with shipping companies,” Nazar said. “The competition is very intense. Kuwait and Qatar have offered larger discounts, reaching up to $35 per barrel.”

Iraqi oil ministry spokesman Salim al-Rikabi said that 70 million barrels of oil were exported from Iraq in August, with revenues of around $4.5bn.

An oil ministry source told Al Jazeera that this was only oil exported from Iraq’s southern oil fields that went through Hormuz.

Iraq continues to export crude through Turkiye using the Iraq–Turkiye Pipeline (ITP). Basra Oil Company manager Bassem Abdul Karim recently said that 250,000 barrels of oil were being transported daily by road from Iraq’s southern oil fields to a storage facility in Kirkuk in northern Iraq.

With sea routes still largely blocked, there are plans to raise volumes to 750,000 barrels.

Last month, Iraq and Turkiye signed a one-year extendable agreement to export at least 750,000 barrels per day through the ITP to the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan, marking a significant step in diversifying Iraq’s export routes.

But industry experts say the Strait of Hormuz remains the only viable long-term solution for Iraq to overcome its financial burden.

“Honestly, Iraq has lagged far behind in finding export alternatives before the crisis in Hormuz began and failed to account for the possibility that it might one day lose its ability to export through the Strait of Hormuz,” Hassan Hafidh, a former OPEC spokesman and specialist in oil and gas affairs, told Al Jazeera.

“All the other alternatives the Iraqis are discussing will not solve their export crisis and the Strait of Hormuz remains at the current time the only way for Iraq to ship the quantities that secure the revenue that Iraq needs.”

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair told parliament last week that the situation in the Strait of Hormuz remains highly unstable and tense.

Iraq could face a sudden blow to its ability to export limited amounts of crude at any time with Iran and the US no closer to reaching a deal to end the war and reopen the strait.

“Even if we can export three million barrels a day right now, there are no guarantees we can sustain this level due to the unpredictable future of the Strait of Hormuz,” Khudhair said.

“If the war drags on, exports will drop. The entire import and export operations hinge on one vital factor, safety in the strait.”
